# PHO Psykiatrisk Akutenhed - Horsens

PHO Psykiatrisk Akutenhed - Horsens is a psychiatric acute-care unit in Horsens, Denmark, appearing in the Danish ADHD quality database's 2024 annual report as a reporting unit for two of the database's clinical quality indicators covering adult ADHD treatment [^src1][^src2].

On Indicator 10 — which measures the share of adult treatment courses in which the patient's need for social support was assessed within 120 days of treatment start — the unit is recorded as achieving 100% fulfillment, though the underlying confidence interval of 16–100 signals an extremely small and uncertain data base [^src1]. This indicator was reported nationally for the first time in the 2024 report, and the steering group behind the ADHD database noted that both the national result (37%) and the regional range (14–52%) fell well short of the 90% quality target, prompting discussion of registration practices and data quality across child/adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals [^src1].

The unit also appears in the results for Indicator 11, which tracks the share of adult treatment courses in which the patient was in ADHD medication treatment within 120 days of starting a care pathway — another measure reported for adults for the first time in 2024, following the ADHD database's 2024 expansion to include adult patients [^src2]. Here PHO Psykiatrisk Akutenhed - Horsens is credited with a 50% result, but again with a very wide confidence interval (1–99), reflecting a thin patient sample [^src2]. The broader Indicator 11 results showed substantial regional variation nationally, ranging from 85% in Region Nordjylland to 37% in Region Hovedstaden, a spread the report attributes largely to differences in registration practice rather than genuine clinical differences [^src2].

Taken together, the two data points illustrate a recurring theme in the 2024 ADHD database report: small reporting units like this one can show extreme percentage results (100% or 50%) that are statistically fragile given very limited numbers of underlying cases, a pattern the steering group flagged as a target for future data-quality improvement [^src1][^src2].
